epic.title: Epic: Physics decomposition — reference laps, driver utilization, segment vocabulary (confirmed spec)
epic.body:
**Shaped-design epic (holding epic).** Reformulate the physics→prediction *payload* as a decomposition: the physics program reassembles its measured capability envelopes into per-car **reference laps** (the modeled car's ideal), and measures each driver as **utilization of their own reference**, conditioned on the circuit's segment composition. Car = reference; driver = utilization. Utilization is explicitly NOT assumed constant per driver — it trends with the circuit's corner-class fingerprint, and the driver's generalized per-class fingerprint supplies the expected-utilization prior.

Spec confirmed by the owner 2026-07-25 via constellation-explorer (work id `explore-ref-utilization`; 3 cycles, 14 excursions incl. 6 prior-art research + 5 in-repo prototypes + 2 design-it-twice panels, 3-lens critic panel, all 28 findings dispositioned). Full confirmed spec body is appended to this issue below the wave list. Exploration record archives to `.agent-work/archive/2026-07-25-explore-ref-utilization/`.

**This epic cuts Build 1 only** (quali-side, 2023-first). Build 2 (race reference: push/managed classification, managed + consistency channels) and Build 3 (live loop: two-speed practice update, seed-then-supersede live maps, physics feature family → fusion choir) have their interfaces ruled in the spec but are deliberately NOT cut here — they are cut after Build 1's instrument panel reports signal sizes.

**Owner rulings binding on every child issue:**
- **No frame-kill.** Weak signal routes to structural work, never abandonment. Sizing outputs steer by *allocation*, not gating.
- **Frozen constants.** Every threshold is pre-registered before the first real-data run (F12 discipline); post-hoc changes require a new named constant set and a full re-run.
- **Pre-quali constraint.** Predictions are made before quali; the quali anchor is post-facto calibration only.
- **Lowest dimensionality that solves the problem**, escalation layers dormant in schemas from day one.
- **No baked-in normality** — Student-t / heavy-tailed forms wherever possible.

**Why a connective epic at all:** this exploration found *five* prior in-repo lineages of this same idea, none joined (circuit rollup #625 validated-but-unwired; #628 utilization pipeline code-complete but never run at season scale; the ephemeris per-corner pilot; apex_obs full-coverage raw material; `segment_classifier.py` complete-but-unwired). Ending that rediscovery loop is itself a goal of this epic — the pipeline is a durable asset regardless of the size of the driver term.

## Relationship to existing work

This epic is deliberately wired into the existing issue graph rather than standing alone — the failure mode it exists to end (five prior lineages of the same idea, each built and then orphaned) is exactly what an unlinked epic reproduces.

**What this feeds:**
- **#450** (Stage-1 Phase 7, physics→evo A/B) — deferred by owner ruling precisely because the payload it would A/B is the thing this epic replaces. Build 1's instrument panel produces the sizing that a re-entered Phase 7 should be designed against. The toggle-gated fusion seam Phase 7 needs is already built (#629 feature view, #630 injection, both merged).
- **#642** (revisit the corner-class count, currently domain-capped at k=4) — that issue is explicitly parked *"once driver-utility/affinity consumers can define what structure matters."* **This epic is that consumer.** Build 1 consumes k=4 as-is; what its per-class replication measures is the evidence #642 has been waiting for.
- **#509** (super-epic: connected physics → prediction pipeline) — this is the composition-phase payload that super-epic's F→C→P arc builds toward.

**What this builds on (landed):** #625 segmentation substrate + #638 its F12 stability rework (the class vocabulary Build 1 consumes); #628 driver utility on the physics basis (the reference-lap path and the strictly-pre anti-circularity convention); #627 unified-basis refit (σ-honesty); #629/#630 (the seam Build 3 targets).

**Known debt that touches this work** (context for implementers, not blockers unless an issue says otherwise): #560 thin-fit acceptance floor; #646 estimates-store re-batch for covariance/σ columns; #632 DB bloat blocking commits; #656 tests dirtying real DBs; #639 the #625 cleanup incl. the undocumented `a_lateral` unit; #587/#559/#577 the fit-store lineage; #650/#648 the thread-cap and launcher-hang taxes on any long run.

issues.title: Pre-register the frozen constant set (braking quantile, lateral-g gate, replication thresholds, sector-calibration coverage)
issues.hitl_reason: Pre-registration is a commitment the owner makes before any real-data run; the whole F12-discipline guarantee is void if an agent picks the numbers after seeing data.
issues.body:
Spec §1 (Build-1 phasing / frozen constants, review T4), §7 (review T6, T11), Testing pathways preamble.

**What to build:** one named, versioned constant module (mirroring `mixture_stability.py`'s `LOG_RADIUS_SCALE` / `LATERAL_G_SCALE` / `F12_AGREEMENT_THRESHOLD` precedent) holding every threshold this epic freezes, each with a one-line rationale and the date/author of the freeze:
- braking-onset robust low quantile (the spec permits p5–p10 — **pick one**, never a range)
- corner lateral-acceleration gate on the field reference lap (v_ref² × curvature)
- min-segment-length sliver-merge threshold (sector cuts exempt)
- residual split-half replication threshold **and** the support-count-scaling formula (§7 / T6)
- composed-sector distribution-calibration coverage criterion, plus the gross-miscalibration sanity bound that makes that check GATING (T11)
- cross-weekend map-stability boundary-drift threshold (§Testing pathways, SegmentMap)

**Acceptance:** the module exists, is imported by every consumer that uses a threshold (no literals at call sites), and carries a docstring stating the discipline: changing a value requires a NEW named constant set and a full re-derivation/re-run, never a silent edit. A test asserts no consumer defines its own copy of a frozen threshold.

**Out of scope:** choosing values by fitting them to data — that is exactly what this issue forbids. Values are chosen from physical reasoning, the existing #638/F12 precedent, and the ephemeris pilot's corner windows.

**HITL:** owner signs off on the values before anything downstream runs.

**Related existing issues:** **#642** — revisiting the corner-class count (k, currently domain-capped at 4) is parked pending exactly this kind of consumer; the frozen constants here are chosen against the *current* k=4 vocabulary, and a future k change is a new named constant set by this issue's own discipline. #638 supplies the validated vocabulary and the F12 threshold precedent this module mirrors.

issues.title: SegmentMap: runtime representation, labeled persistence, and versioned store
issues.body:
Spec §1, interface bullet (design-it-twice three-way hybrid; full candidate texts in the archived `excursions/D2-segmap-{min,flex,caller}-RESULT.md`).

**Candidate labels used below** (each design-it-twice candidate was written under a different constraint): **CALLER** = optimized for the hot call site; **FLEX** = optimized for schema evolution and safe re-indexing; **MINIMAL** = optimized for the smallest possible interface surface.

**What to build — exactly the hybrid the spec rules, no re-litigation:**
- **Runtime (CALLER candidate):** flat parallel numpy arrays — boundaries, lengths, int8 type/sector/direction codes, corner descriptors, a severity-membership matrix. Never a list of objects. `segment_of(distances)` is one `searchsorted` with wrap-modulo on the closed loop; out-of-range never raises. The MC race sim fetches three read-only arrays once — zero per-draw cost. `reclassify_severity(mixture)` decouples geometry from classification: a mixture refit is an O(n_corners) membership recompute, never a geometry rebuild, and vice versa.
- **Identity & persistence (FLEX candidate):** *labels, never positions.* Memberships persist as tidy rows keyed by `vocabulary_id` / `class_id` strings minted once at fit time (`VocabularyRef` registry); era refits and k-changes are pure inserts — no migration, no index-shift corruption. At load, labeled rows materialize into the caller-shaped positional matrix plus a `class_ids` column map; the conversion happens **exactly once** per load.
- **Version axes exercised in Build 1 (review S6):** weekend key, layout identity (content-hash of geometry-only cut points, deliberately excluding sector-forced splits), vocabulary fit version. The per-weekend supersede chain is trivially v1 in batch mode; format version lives in the store convention.
- **Lifecycle (MINIMAL candidate), Build-1 phasing per review S3:** the single deep write entry point carries the whole cold/seeded/superseded compare-and-branch in its *interface*, but **Build 1 implements the cold/historical path only** — the seeded/supersede branch ships with Build 3 when live weekends exist. Three narrow reads with deliberately distinct miss-contracts: current and by-version raise loudly; latest-for-seeding returns `None` on a genuine cold start. No update/patch surface anywhere. Supersede requires a recorded contradiction reason. Provenance carries config fingerprint + FIA doc citations.
- **Convergent, adopted without debate:** adjacency computed, never persisted; sub-phases marks-only and dormant (`resolution="subphase"` reserved in the signature, backing store deferred — and single-homed HERE, not duplicated in the fingerprint address space, per review S5); no aggregate-statistics methods on the map (rollups are consumer-side); **no grip state in the map** (grip mutates session-by-session, the map versions weekend-by-weekend); the severity mixture is consumed as a fitted input behind a Protocol so a Student-t swap never touches SegmentMap.

**Acceptance:** unit tests for the searchsorted hot path (incl. wrap and out-of-range), the load-boundary conversion round-trip, label-stability under a simulated class reorder (the corruption class this design exists to prevent), and the read miss-contracts.

**Out of scope:** the derivation logic itself (issue C), any grip coupling, live seeding.

issues.title: Per-weekend segment-map derivation: complete tiling, FIA sector nesting, severity membership
issues.body:
Spec §1 (canonical gate, severity ladder, nesting) + Testing pathways / SegmentMap.

**Every threshold named below is imported from issue A's frozen-constants module — never a literal at the call site, never a value picked here.**

**What to build:**
- **Canonical gate, computed off the FIELD REFERENCE LAP, not per-lap:** corner segment = reference-lap lateral acceleration (v_ref² × curvature) above the frozen threshold; braking zone = field-**envelope** brake onset at the frozen robust low quantile (**never a mean** — a mean onset sits inside the real braking zone; the median-pooled-ribbon failure is the documented precedent — see `excursions/x2-RESULT.md` in the archived exploration record) running to corner entry; straight = the remainder via the straight-arc grouper. Per-lap kinematic gates are demoted to **observation filters** — the map is fixed per weekend and every lap is scored against it, so driver-invariance holds by construction.
- **Nesting:** derive FIA sector lines per weekend by time-to-distance interpolation (pooled median, sub-meter). Sector lines are **mandatory cut points**: a straddling segment SPLITS into same-class pieces — never snapped (snapping distorts physical boundaries). Sector-nesting fails CLOSED (`SectorLineUnavailableError`) rather than emitting a map without the invariant. Sliver merging exempts sector cuts.
- **Severity membership:** Build 1 **consumes the existing validated class vocabulary** (#638 artifacts, F12 PASS 5/5). Memberships stay SOFT — fractional weights flow through every consumer. The per-era Student-t refit + fresh F12 gate run at backfill, when multi-era circuit diversity makes the gate meaningful (review T10 — an open deferral, stated, not silent).
- Populate the map's ACTIVE attributes: adjacency (neighbor class, following-straight length, direction flip — computed, never persisted) and turn direction (an int8 code in the runtime array). **Sub-phase marks stay DORMANT through Build 1** — reserve the marks-only signature exactly as issue B does; do not build a backing store or populate them.

**Acceptance — note the honest test labels (review T3):** tiling completeness and sector-nesting exactness are **construction checks** (they catch coverage and arithmetic bugs, not mis-typing). The substantive GATING checks are:
1. **cross-weekend map stability** — boundary drift between same-circuit weekends within the frozen threshold;
2. **typing spot-checks** against independently-derived references — the ephemeris pilot's Bahrain corner windows (`excursions/P4-RESULT.md`) and the corner tallies recorded in the #625 circuit-rollup artifacts.
Falsified by unstable or physically wrong maps, not merely by gaps.

**Out of scope:** cross-year corner history; per-corner identity beyond arc-length within a layout version; live seeding.

**Related existing issues:** **#639** — cleanup of the #625 substrate this issue builds on, including a **duplicated fallback path and an undocumented `a_lateral` unit**. Read it before writing the lateral-acceleration gate: an ambiguous unit convention in the substrate is a silent way to mis-type every corner. **#642** — the k=4 cap this issue consumes as-is.

issues.title: Grip baseline module G: cumulative-car-lap evolution curve + free inter-session offsets
issues.body:
Spec §2.

**What to build:** ONE canonical module owning per-weekend track grip state, so every consumer subtracts an identical G (this ends the half-implementation scatter that currently exists across the repo).
- **Intra-session:** saturating evolution curve indexed on **cumulative car-laps**, not wall clock.
- **Inter-session:** a free offset per session start, estimated from data — it absorbs overnight change, support-series running (support laps are invisible to our data by construction and must land in the offset), and temperature. A rain flag forces offset re-estimation with wide σ.
- **Fit:** from field-pooled pace with compound / tyre-age / fuel correction via the existing machinery (`src/physics/layer2/tyre_supplant.py`); Student-t residuals; σ(G) propagates to every consumer.
- Escalation layer, dormant: per-class evolution curves.
- Interface follows the repo's existing estimate-store pattern (`src/physics/layer2/estimate_store.py` + `estimate_batch.py`: fit artifact + query surface); design-it-twice deliberately skipped — precedented shape, not novel.

**Acceptance — GATING, and specifically NOT in-sample (review T1/T2):**
1. **Held-out reconciliation:** G is fit on a subset of drivers/laps and scored on the **disjoint remainder** — same driver/compound/similar-fuel laps must reconcile across sessions after subtracting G. In-sample self-scoring is explicitly rejected: with two free fit surfaces per weekend, an almost-arbitrary G improves in-sample error by absorbing noise, so the in-sample check only fires on a badly broken fit, never a subtly wrong one.
2. **Synthetic-recovery / identifiability test:** inject a known ground-truth curve + known session offsets into simulated pace; the fit must recover them **separably**. The curve's initial value and the session offset are aliased in principle — if they are not separable, σ(G) is structurally understated everywhere downstream.
Falsified if held-out reconciliation fails to improve, or synthetic recovery fails to separate.

**Out of scope:** per-class curves (dormant escalation); anything that writes grip state into SegmentMap.

**Related existing issues:** **#560** (thin fits pass acceptance with no minimum-flying-laps/sample floor) — the same thin-session problem lands directly on G's field-pooled fit, and the powered F10 run has already surfaced real sessions with no usable flying laps for the back-of-grid cars. Decide explicitly what G does with a session too thin to fit, rather than letting it through. #650 (the blanket physics thread cap roughly doubles fit wall-time) is worth knowing before estimating this issue's compute.

issues.title: Reference laps as a first-class product + class-grain utilization observables store (time and energy channels)
issues.body:
Spec §3.

**What to build:**
- **Reference laps via the existing production path** (#628 Path B): causal `build_car_ceiling` (strictly-pre, anti-circular) → `simulate_lap`. The **scalar ideal lap time becomes a first-class stored product** — it is currently computed and discarded. Frontier discipline is confirmed on 4/5 views; coast feeds no utilization axis.
- **Circuit fingerprint = true per-class TIME-shares** taken from the FIELD-REFERENCE car's simulated lap (this retires the #625 distance-share caveat). Each car's own reference still baselines its own utilization.
- **The season-scale utilization run** — the #628 rerun that has never actually happened: per-driver, per-segment-class observables, **G-subtracted**, persisted with `map_version`. Time-ledger native (transit-time deficits). Speed profiles kept diagnostic. Per-segment **energy** tracked in BOTH channels for §7's pre-registered comparison, with honest scope: relative deployment vs the car's own rolling baseline + phase structure + derate flags — **never absolute SOC or kW** (the 2026 rampdown regulation makes deployment signatures curved ramps, not cliffs).
- **Asymmetric channel treatment, ruled:** straights are car-rich / driver-thin (slipstream confound — the existing negative-control finding); braking zones are driver-rich.
- Store mirrors the existing `driver_utility_observables` schema plus class and map-version columns; design-it-twice skipped — precedented shape.
- **Units are absolute deficit (m/s), never a ratio** — #628's anti-circularity-hardened convention.

**Acceptance — GATING:** deficits-sum-to-lap is a **construction check** (review T5 — it cannot catch misattribution between classes). The substantive check is **attribution robustness**: per-class deficits stay stable under boundary jitter within the frozen quantile's uncertainty (jackknife over derivation laps).

**Out of scope:** race-side observables (Build 2); absolute ERS/SOC inference; any fingerprint fitting.

**Related existing issues:** **#646** — `physics_estimates.db` was built pre-#627 and its cross-view covariance / σ-honesty columns are unpopulated; if this issue's reference laps read those columns, that re-batch is a real prerequisite, so check before assuming the store is complete. #559/#577/#587 are the fit-store lineage (stale baseline, re-batch, retire-or-demote) — relevant to which store this reads from. #632 (DB bloat via `processed_telemetry`) matters if this run writes anywhere near the f1_data DBs.

issues.title: Validate the pooling primitive under realistic driver×class imbalance (decides fit_two_way vs direct-pooling fallback)
issues.body:
Spec §4, statistical-core bullet (review T9). **Small, decisive, and it gates the fingerprint fit** — run it before building G's consumer.

**The problem:** the spec's hierarchy (field mean → driver-overall → class cell, + a class-across-drivers parent) maps *plausibly* onto the existing `fit_two_way` primitive in `src/physics/layer2/pooling.py` with axes reinterpreted as driver×class. But `fit_two_way` is a two-way crossed decomposition using method-of-moments variance components that its own docstring calls **"exact for a balanced grid, approximate otherwise"** — and driver×class support is decidedly unbalanced (thin support in rare corner classes; class counts vary with the circuit mix across a season). The existing driver-facing precedent, #628's `driver_utility.py`, does NOT use `fit_two_way` at all — it pools per-(driver, axis) groups directly through `pool_random_effects` with no crossed second axis. Reusing it here is a **new application**, not free reuse, and the spec demotes it to a *candidate* primitive pending exactly this test.

**What to build:** a synthetic-recovery harness — known ground-truth driver effects and class effects, injected into deliberately unbalanced cell counts drawn to match the real 2023 driver×class support profile. **That profile comes from data that already exists** — per-driver lap counts in the 2023 DB crossed with the #625/#638 class tallies — NOT from this epic's own pipeline output, which is why this issue has no predecessors and can run immediately, in parallel with the store build. Score shrinkage behaviour and variance-component recovery.

**Acceptance:** a written verdict, either way, with the imbalance profile stated:
- **PASS** → `fit_two_way` is adopted for the fingerprint hierarchy;
- **FAIL** → the named fallback is adopted instead: #628-style direct per-(driver, class) pooling with explicit parent shrinkage.
Either outcome is a complete, successful deliverable — the point is that the choice is *measured*, not assumed. Thin-support → fat-tail behaviour goes through the repo's canonical Student-t seam (`predictive_t`, project-wide ν defaults) in both branches; no invented statistical machinery in Build 1.

**Out of scope:** a true hierarchical-t upgrade (possible later behind the same interface); anything touching real data.

issues.title: DriverFingerprint: versioned cell store + hierarchical shrinkage fit (both channels, strictly-pre)
issues.body:
Spec §4 (design-it-twice three-way hybrid; full candidate texts in the archived `excursions/D2-fp-{min,flex,caller}-RESULT.md`).

**Candidate labels used below:** **CALLER** = optimized for the hot call site; **FLEX** = optimized for schema evolution and safe re-indexing; **MINIMAL** = optimized for the smallest possible interface surface.

**What to build:**
- **Cells:** per (driver, rules-era), class-level utilization cells (mean, σ, support n), fit by hierarchical Student-t shrinkage — field mean → driver-overall → class cell, plus a class-across-drivers parent — recency-weighted. Primitive chosen by issue F's verdict. **Slow-offline-loop mutation only**: fingerprints never move during a weekend, and no fit-on-read path exists to make that structural rather than a convention.
- **Vocabulary:** **corner-severity classes only — straights are excluded** per the existing confounded-negative-control ruling. Composition vectors therefore sum to the corner share, not 1.0. (The distance-vs-time-share provenance flag is dropped from the production path per review S11 — legacy tag only if #625-era data is ever joined.)
- **Address space (FLEX candidate, trimmed per S1/S5/S10):** a versioned `CellAddress` — era, class-vocabulary version, class id — plus the dormant `channel` dimension (`"utilization"` today, `"energy"` when §7's comparison activates it) and what-measure slot strings (push / managed / consistency / management-efficiency — the last is the owner-named Build-2 ambitious measure: how much lap time a driver gives up per unit of tyre/energy saved; defined in the archived `IDEAS_BOARD.md`, reserved here, unused in Build 1). Escalations are inserts, never migrations. Segment-discriminativeness lives in fit-time observable weighting — zero address cost. **Sub-phase and transition dimensions are NOT duplicated here** — single-homed in SegmentMap (issue B); if they activate, addressing derives them from the map's vocabulary then. `ClassVocabulary` carries the F12 stability verdict and fitting against a failed-gate vocabulary is refused by default (explicit override only). Tidy persistence with a canonical non-NULL `cell_key` (the SQLite NULL-PK gotcha designed around).
- **Discipline (MINIMAL candidate):** `as_of_round` is **REQUIRED with no default** — the strictly-pre causal cutoff applied to the driver side, citing #628's measured **14.6×-materiality leakage precedent**. A full-era retrospective passes a cutoff past the era's end; there is no "no cutoff" mode. Thinness is priced ONCE at fit time (σ widening) — never re-filtered downstream. Era and vocabulary mismatches refuse loudly, never silently substitute. Persistence is replace-on-rerun. Every fingerprint is always fully populated: exactly k cells, `unresolved` status rather than missing rows.
- **Fit BOTH channels** (time-deficit and energy) so §7's pre-registered comparison has something to compare.
- Rules-era key = the existing `RegulationEra.for_season` seam.

**Acceptance:** cutoff-leakage test (a fit with a cutoff cannot see post-cutoff rows); thin-cell σ-widening priced once and only once; loud refusal on era/vocabulary mismatch; k-cells-always-populated invariant.

**Out of scope:** the join (issue H); race-side push/managed cells (Build 2); low-rank factorization (shelved — the read boundary deliberately carries no factorization hook).

**Related existing issues:** **#560** (thin fits pass as ok, no sample floor) — the direct sibling of this issue's thin-cell problem, one layer down. This issue prices thinness once at fit time via σ widening; #560 asks whether a thin fit should have been accepted at all. Worth reconciling the two answers rather than having each layer solve it differently. **#642** — what this issue's per-class replication measures is the evidence #642 is waiting for on the k question.

issues.title: The join: circuit composition × fingerprint → weekend utilization prior, with reduces-to-simple-case invariants
issues.body:
Spec §4, the join bullet — **this is the core product of Build 1**.

**What to build:** circuit per-class time-share vector × fingerprint cells, soft-membership-weighted, producing an expected weekend utilization prior with honest σ (thin cells → fat σ). **The linear join IS the prior** — escalation to sequence or bespoke formulations happens only if simple arithmetic under-explains. Thin exposure is surfaced explicitly (`thin_classes` / `weight_on_thin` fields), never silently discounted. Every cross-boundary call pins the class-vocabulary version. The join is reserved for the practice update and fusion summaries; the race simulator and the instrument panel read **un-aggregated cells** directly.

**Acceptance — GATING unit invariants (review T7). These exist because an outcome-level win can hide a mechanically broken join:** a wrong per-class weight, a sign error on a subset of cells, or wrong σ-widening can still beat a driver-overall-only baseline on average through compensating errors, since overall skill dominates the signal (xR3's golf-analog finding).
1. Uniform composition across classes ⇒ the join returns exactly the driver-overall mean.
2. All cells identical ⇒ the join returns that constant regardless of the composition vector.
3. Single-class circuit ⇒ σ propagation collapses to that cell's σ.
4. Soft memberships flow through unchanged; composition sums to the corner share, not 1.0.

**Out of scope:** whether the join *beats* the driver-overall prior — that is a DIAGNOSTIC sizing measurement in issue K, deliberately not a correctness gate here.

issues.title: Instrument panel: variance decomposition, residual split-half replication (per channel), composed-sector scorecard
issues.body:
Spec §7 — Build 1's exit instrument. **Sizing, never go/no-go**: outputs carry named *allocation* decisions, and by owner ruling no output halts the program.

**What to build:**
1. **Variance decomposition** — segment-time variance split into car-reference / driver-utilization / residual shares (the driver share reads as a **floor**). This is THE "set the size" instrument; its output directs where Build-2 effort goes.
2. **Residual split-half replication** — per-class fingerprint replication computed **after removing overall skill** (the golf-corrected form). Raw replication flatters by smuggling overall skill back in; the mature analog found residual shape-fit had *zero* out-of-sample power once overall skill was controlled, so this correction is load-bearing, not cosmetic. Doubles as a σ-honesty check (do cells replicate within their stated uncertainty?). Thresholds and the support-count-scaling formula come from issue A, frozen pre-run.
3. **Pre-registered channel comparison (owner-initiated):** run the replication per class in BOTH channels — time-deficit and energy (kinetic-energy deficit from the same speed observables). **Whichever channel replicates better in a class earns join weight there.** Registered before any real-data run. Rationale: time weights segments by lap-time cost (driver-signal-aligned); energy natively expresses momentum-carry and deployment (car- and 2026-aligned) — the comparison decides empirically instead of on priors.
4. **Composed-sector scorecard** — segment predictions sum into FIA sectors and are validated against **official sector times already on disk**, every pipeline weekend: central values AND distribution-calibration coverage. Per review T11 the two claims are separated: position-sum exactness is a construction check; the genuine external anchor is predicted sector-time distribution calibration — DIAGNOSTIC for signal size, GATING only on the frozen gross-miscalibration sanity bound.

**Acceptance:** the panel runs end-to-end and emits a written, versioned report with all four instruments and the constants it used.

**Out of scope:** any gate that halts Build 2 or 3 on a signal size.

issues.title: 3-circuit end-to-end pilot slice (tracer bullet) before any season-scale run
issues.body:
Spec §8, Build 1 opening (review S8).

**Why this exists:** the exploration found five prior in-repo lineages of this exact idea that were each built and then **never joined or run at season scale**. Committing straight to a full 2023 season before a single end-to-end signal repeats that pattern with a bigger, slower-to-falsify bet.

**What to build:** run the whole chain — tiling → G → utilization → fingerprint-fit smoke → **the join** → panel dry-run — on **three contrasting 2023 circuits** (pick for genuine contrast: a high-severity-corner venue, a low-downforce/straight-dominated venue, and a street circuit). Wire the stages together as one invocable pipeline, not five scripts run by hand.

**Acceptance:** one command produces, for all three circuits: valid maps, a fitted G with its held-out score, populated utilization observables, a smoke-fit fingerprint, and a panel dry-run. Every GATING check from issues C/D/E/H passes on the slice. A short written report names anything that broke and what it implies for the season run.

**Out of scope:** interpreting signal sizes (three circuits cannot size anything) — this slice tests that the machine *runs*, not what it says.

**Related existing issues:** **#656** (the test suite writes to the real `data/f1_data_*.db` files instead of an isolated fixture) — this issue runs a full pipeline end-to-end and must not inherit that habit; use explicit DB paths. #650/#648 (thread cap, launcher hang under detached start) are the standing taxes on any long unattended run.

issues.title: Season-scale 2023 run + panel report + owner allocation decisions
issues.hitl_reason: Two human checkpoints, not one. BEFORE the run: an explicit go/no-go on committing to season-scale compute (expensive, long, rate-limit exposed) once the 3-circuit pilot reports. AFTER the run: the panel's outputs carry allocation decisions that are the owner's to make — which channel earns join weight where, where Build-2 effort goes, and whether reference-lap fidelity work precedes fingerprint work.
issues.body:
Spec §8, Build 1 body + §7 outputs.

**Checkpoint BEFORE starting (review finding):** the pilot (issue J) reports first; the owner gives an explicit go before any season-scale compute is committed. Season-scale runs here are long and rate-limit exposed — starting one is a decision, not a default.

**What to run:** the full 2023 season through the pipeline — vocabulary tilings → G → season-scale class-grain utilization (including scalar reference-lap recovery) → fingerprint fit + join → instrument panel. 2023 because every store is deepest there.

**Deliverable:** the panel report, plus a DIAGNOSTIC held-out-weekend comparison — fingerprint×composition prior vs a driver-overall-only prior (the golf null is the benchmark to beat; the join's *correctness* is already established by issue H's unit invariants, not by this comparison).

**The three allocation decisions the owner takes from the report:**
1. variance shares → where Build-2 effort goes;
2. per-class, per-channel replication → which fingerprint axes (and which channel) earn join weight;
3. sector calibration → whether reference-lap fidelity work precedes fingerprint work.

**Explicitly NOT a gate.** By owner ruling there is no frame-kill: a small or fat-σ driver term routes to structural work (different observables, different conditioning), never to abandonment. A measured negative here is a complete, successful deliverable and should be reported as one.

**Out of scope:** backfill of 2019–2026 (chased only after the panel proves the machine); Build 2 and Build 3 work.

**Related existing issues:** **#632** (f1_data DBs bloat to ~2GB via `processed_telemetry`, which blocks DB commits) and **#656** (tests dirty the real DBs) both bear on a season-scale run: know what this writes and where before starting. #650 (thread cap ≈2× fit wall-time) is the reason a season-scale estimate built on older timings will be optimistic — the powered F10 run overran its own 8.4h projection for exactly this reason.
